items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Unc, as we called him, Harry Waters. He was supposed to be some kin to Ethel Waters. He was an older man then, and I guess he's passed on.

ctx.x: He was very good, but he loved Philadelphia and he started raising a family there and then he never got out.

Then there was a fellow, he's still in Philadelphia, he's still living, was, Henry Branch. Henry Branch played the guitar. But, Unc, as we called him, Harry Waters. He was supposed to be some kin to Ethel Waters. He was an older man then, and I guess he's passed on.
Well, in 1918, when you were back at the Madhouse, the first jazz recordings have come out by then. By the Original Dixieland Jazz Band. This white group from New Orleans, do you remember?
